2027-08-06.title: The Transfiguration of Our Lord
readings: His face shone like the sun
Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord?
The Lord will be your everlasting light
We were eyewitnesses of his majesty
O the depth of the riches and wisdom of God
This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him
2027-08-06.alt: Feast of the Transfiguration (M'thale). The season of the Transfiguration begins. The Fifteen Days' Fast continues until 15 August.
2027-08-06.verse: Then from the cloud came a voice that said, “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
theo: Jesus takes Peter, John and James up the mountain to pray. “And while he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothes became dazzling white.” Moses and Elijah appear in glory and speak with him “of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.” The Law and the Prophets bear witness to Christ, and they speak of the Cross. The glory of Tabor and the darkness of Calvary belong together.

Peter, overwhelmed, says: “Master, it is good for us to be here; let us make three dwellings, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” The Old Testament reading recalls the Feast of Booths, when Israel lived in tents to remember God's care in the desert. But a cloud overshadows them, the cloud of God's presence, and a voice says: “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!” When the voice has spoken, “Jesus was found alone.” He is the true dwelling of God among us.

At Sinai God came down on the mountain in fire and cloud, and the people could not approach. On Tabor the glory of God shines in the face of a man, and the disciples are touched by him: “Get up and do not be afraid.” St Peter later writes that he and the others “were eyewitnesses of his majesty… we ourselves heard this voice come from heaven, while we were with him on the holy mountain.” Our faith rests on what the apostles saw and heard.

The Transfiguration shows us our own future. The light that shone from Christ is the glory he will share with those who belong to him. Isaiah says: “The LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.” Paul can only exclaim: “O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!” In the season that now begins, the Church contemplates the glory of Christ and prepares for his coming.
conn: Exodus 19–20: God speaks from the mountain; Tabor: the Father speaks of the Son.
Deuteronomy 16: the Feast of Booths; Peter's three tents; Christ is God's true tent among us (John 1:14).
Psalm 24:3–4: “Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD?… Those who have clean hands and pure hearts.”
Isaiah 60:19: no need of sun or moon; the Lord is our light.
altar: What the three apostles saw on the mountain we receive veiled at the altar. The same Christ who shone on Tabor is present in the Holy Mysteries; one day the veil will be lifted, and we shall see him as he is.
outline: The light he will share with us.
“This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
live: Spend fifteen minutes in silent prayer today, perhaps before the Blessed Sacrament.
Choose one word of Jesus to obey this week.
Continue the Fifteen Days' Fast with joy, in honour of Mary.
fathers: The principal purpose of the Transfiguration was to remove the scandal of the Cross from the disciples' hearts, so that the humiliation of his voluntary suffering would not disturb the faith of those to whom the glory of his hidden dignity had been revealed (Sermon 51, 3).
“It is good for us to be here.” Let us hasten there with confidence and joy, to enter the cloud like Moses and Elijah, or like James and John (Homily on the Transfiguration).
magis: The Transfiguration gives a foretaste of Christ's glorious coming; the whole Trinity appears: the Father in the voice, the Son in the man, the Spirit in the shining cloud.
Christ's Transfiguration aims at strengthening the apostles' faith in anticipation of his Passion.
Our sharing in Christ's glory is the hope of the resurrection.
saints: Sunday 8 August: I Sunday after the Transfiguration. 10 August: St Lawrence. 14 August: St Maximilian Kolbe. Sunday 15 August: Shunoyo, the Assumption of Mary, Mother of God.
2027-08-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, transfigured on the holy mountain, you showed your disciples the glory that was yours before the Cross. Teach us to listen to you, to go up the mountain in prayer, and to come down again to serve; and bring us at last to see your face in the light that never fades. Amen.

quick: Jesus is transfigured while praying; the Law and the Prophets speak of his Cross.
“This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
The light of Tabor is the glory Christ will share with us.
2027-08-06.action: Spend fifteen minutes in silent prayer today.
2027-08-06.question: Do I really listen to Jesus?
2027-08-06.special: Transfiguration of Our Lord (Friday). The season of the Transfiguration begins.
illus: Pilgrims climb Mount Tabor in Galilee to the Basilica of the Transfiguration. At the top the view opens over the whole valley. Prayer does that: it lifts us up to see our lives as God sees them.

family.explain: On a mountain Jesus' face shone like the sun, and God the Father said: “This is my Son. Listen to him!”
family.intention: We pray to listen to Jesus every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What is Jesus asking our family to do?”

kidsaint: A deacon in Rome who took care of the poor. When the emperor demanded the Church's treasures, Lawrence brought the poor and said: “These are the treasures of the Church.” He was martyred in 258. Lesson: the poor are the Church's treasure.
term: The name used in the Syro-Malankara lectionary for the feast of the Transfiguration (6 August). The Syriac word is generally linked with “tents” or “booths”, recalling Peter's three tents and the Feast of Booths.
termMore: The sixth season of the Syro-Malankara year, from 6 August to the feast of the Holy Cross (14 September): a time to contemplate Christ's glory and prepare for his final coming.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus took Peter, John and James up a mountain to pray. And while he was praying, his face changed and his clothes became dazzling white. For a moment the disciples saw who he really is: the Son of God, full of glory.

Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with him. About what? About “his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem”, that is, his Passion and death. On the mountain of glory they speak of the Cross. The Transfiguration was given to strengthen the disciples, so that when they saw Jesus disfigured on Calvary they would remember Tabor.

Peter wanted to stay: “It is good for us to be here; let us make three tents.” But a cloud covered them, and the Father spoke: “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!” Then they saw only Jesus. The Christian life is not about staying on the mountain; it is about listening to Jesus and going down with him to serve.

The light of Tabor is also our future. St Paul says we shall be changed into his likeness. Every Holy Qurbono is a little Tabor: we go up to the altar, we see the Lord with the eyes of faith, and we come down to live his word. Today, climb the mountain: spend fifteen minutes in silence with the Lord, and listen to him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus went up a mountain with three friends. While he prayed, his face shone like the sun and his clothes became bright white!
Then a cloud came and God the Father said: “This is my Son. Listen to him!”
How can we listen to Jesus? By reading the Bible and doing what he says. Let's be good listeners!

intro: Theme: “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
On the mountain the glory of the Son shines through his humanity. Moses and Elijah speak with him about his departure in Jerusalem. The glory is revealed to strengthen the disciples for the Cross.

sub: Moses' face shone after speaking with God; Jesus' face shines with his own divine glory.
The Transfiguration reveals who Jesus is: true God and true man.
It also shows what we are called to become: transformed by grace.
q: Moses came down from Mount Sinai. As he came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hand, Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became dazzling white.
points.apply: Spend time in prayer before the Lord this week, and let him change you.

sub: Moses promised a prophet like himself, whom the people must heed.
The Father's voice confirms: Jesus is that Prophet and more, the beloved Son.
Moses and Elijah, the Law and the Prophets, point to him.
q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
Then from the cloud came a voice that said, “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
points.apply: Before each decision this week ask: what does Jesus say about this?

sub: On the mountain they speak of his “departure”: his Passion in Jerusalem.
The disciples see the glory so that they will not lose faith when they see the Cross.
Isaiah's promise is fulfilled: the Lord himself is our everlasting light.
q: The sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give light to you by night; but the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Offer one present suffering to the Lord, trusting that it leads to glory.

concl: The Transfiguration gives us a glimpse of Easter in the middle of the journey to the Cross.
Let us listen to the Son and let his light transform us.
2027-08-06.resolve: Keep the rest of the Fifteen Days' Fast faithfully, with Mary.
